title: Directed colimits of ring sheaves compute the underlying module colimit on a site
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site essentially small in a coefficient universe $w$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of unital commutative rings on it. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset in $w$ and let $(A_i,a_{ij})_{i\leq j}$ be a diagram of sheaves of unital commutative rings, with compatible unital ring-sheaf maps $s_i:R\to A_i$, so $a_{ij}s_i=s_j$. Suppose a cocone of unital ring-sheaf maps $q_i:A_i\to A$ is a colimit in the category of sheaves of unital commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and a unital map $s:R\to A$ satisfies $q_i s_i=s$ for every $i$. Give $A_i$ and $A$ their $R$-module sheaf structures by $r\cdot x=s_i(r)x$ and $r\cdot x=s(r)x$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the underlying $R$-module sheaf $A$, with these same maps $q_i$, is a colimit of the underlying $R$-module sheaves $A_i$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Explicitly, for every $R$-module sheaf $M$ and compatible $R$-linear maps $f_i:A_i\to M$, there is a unique $R$-linear map $f:A\to M$ with $f q_i=f_i$ for every $i$. All ring sheaves, module sheaves, and the object and morphism sets of $I$ lie in $w$; the site universes may differ from $w$.

proof.text: Use scalar compatibility to view every transition map and every leg of q as a morphism between the restricted regular R-module sheaves. The formula is the original ring map on sections; multiplicativity and compatibility with the scalar map prove linearity. These maps form a diagram D and a cocone d whose underlying abelian diagram and cocone are definitionally the images of A and q under forgetting rings to abelian groups.

Put U = forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat ⋙ forget₂ RingCat AddCommGrpCat. U preserves limits and filtered colimits. On the w-small model of C, Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.instPreservesSheafification therefore shows that U preserves sheafification. The instance in Sites.Equivalence transports this to C; its required structured-arrow limits exist because these index categories are essentially w-small (hasLimitsOfShape_of_essentiallySmall). The same site transport provides ring and abelian sheafification and the abelian WEqualsLocallyBijective criterion. The natural isomorphism sheafComposeNatIso identifies presheaf sheafification followed by sheafCompose J U with postcomposition by U followed by abelian sheafification. The latter preserves I-colimits. Applying Adjunction.preservesColimitsOfShape_iff to the fully faithful sheafification adjunction proves that sheafCompose J U preserves I-colimits.

proof.text: The image of q under sheafCompose J U is thus an abelian-sheaf colimit, by isColimitOfPreserves. By lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful, module-sheaf colimits of shape I exist and their forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves them. This functor reflects isomorphisms, so reflectsColimit_of_reflectsIsomorphisms and isColimitOfReflects show that d is a module-sheaf colimit.

proof.text: Package the compatible f_i as a cocone c on D. Define f = hd.desc c for the colimit proof hd of d. The equations hd.fac c i, evaluated on sections, give exactly the requested factorization. If f′ has the same sectionwise composites, extensionality of module-sheaf maps gives d.ι.app i ≫ f′ = c.ι.app i. The uniqueness clause hd.uniq then gives f′ = f.
